mainTopic: The order of the morning קטורת and the הטבת הנרות, and how the תמיד's blood is sprinkled according to רבי שמעון איש המצפה
overview: This amud opens in the middle of the גמרא's explanation of a מחלוקת between the רבנן and אבא שאול. The question is whether the morning קטורת comes before or after the הטבה, the cleaning of the מנורה's lamps. The רבנן prove from the afternoon פסוק, together with a ברייתא, that 'when he cleans the lamps' means 'at the time of', not 'after'. אבא שאול rejects that proof: the afternoon is a special case because of the word 'אותו'. רב פפא then resolves a contradiction between two משניות by assigning one to the רבנן and the other to אבא שאול. He accepts that this leaves one משנה split between the two opinions. The גמרא explains why אביי and רב פפא each chose their own answer. Next, with 'גופא', the גמרא turns to the sprinkling of blood. רבי שמעון איש המצפה says the תמיד's blood is given half like an עולה and half like a חטאת, based on a פסוק. The גמרא tests other possible methods and rejects them, and it is in the middle of answering a challenge from the word 'טהרו' when the amud ends.

steps.title: The רבנן's reading: burn the קטורת at the time of the הטבה
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that the פסוק means the קטורת is burned at the time of the הטבה, not necessarily after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time of cleaning the lamps, the incense should be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the רבנן's explanation of the morning פסוק. In their reading, 'when he cleans the lamps, he shall burn the קטורת' means 'around the same time', not 'afterward'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול reads the פסוק as a sequence: first the הטבה, then the קטורת. The רבנן read it as a time marker: the קטורת belongs to the time period of the הטבה. Their reading leaves room for the קטורת to come first.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה

steps.confusionAlert: 'בעידן' does not mean 'after'. It means 'at the time of'. The whole argument depends on this difference.

phrases.english: At the time of the cleaning of the lamps, the incense shall be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's explanation, begun on the previous amud, of the reasoning of the רבנן against אבא שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The morning קטורת is tied to the time of the הטבה, not required to come after it.

steps.title: Proof from the afternoon verse about lighting the lamps
steps.stepSummary: If 'when he does X, he burns the קטורת' meant 'after X', then in the afternoon the lamps would have to be lit before the קטורת. That conclusion is hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, then in the afternoon, where it is written 'And when אהרן lights the lamps in the afternoon he shall burn it', would it also mean that he first lights the lamps and only then burns the afternoon קטורת?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the רבנן's reading by showing where the opposite reading leads. It points to a matching afternoon פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning and afternoon פסוקים are built the same way: 'when he does something to the lamps, he burns the קטורת.' If the morning פסוק meant 'first the lamps, then the קטורת', the afternoon פסוק would have to mean the same thing. The next step shows that this cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so
When he lights (literally, raises up the flame)

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
then in the afternoon, where it is written:
"And when Aaron lights the lamps
in the afternoon he shall burn it,"
would it also be that first he lights the lamps

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר מַקְטִיר קְטוֹרֶת שֶׁל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם?!
phrases.english: and only then burns the afternoon incense?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking; he means this order couldn't possibly be right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading in Step 1 by showing that the opposite reading leads to a problem.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's reading that 'when' means 'at the time of', not 'after'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel afternoon פסוק (שמות ל:ח), 'ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות בין הערבים יקטירנה'.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows lighting the מנורה is the last service of the day
steps.stepSummary: If someone accepts that the afternoon lighting comes before the קטורת, a ברייתא blocks that answer. It teaches that lighting the מנורה is the one service done from evening to morning, so nothing comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that yes, it is so, was it not taught in a ברייתא: 'From evening until morning' means give the lamp its full measure of oil, so it keeps burning all night from evening until morning. Another explanation: 'From evening until morning' means you have no service that is valid from evening until morning except this one alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible escape. Someone might answer, 'Fine, in the afternoon the lamps really are lit first.' The ברייתא shows that this cannot be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says lighting the מנורה is the only עבודה that fits 'from evening to morning'. That means it is the final service of the day. So in the afternoon the קטורת must come before the lighting, and 'when he lights... he burns' cannot mean 'after'.

keyTerms.meaning: Give it its proper measure (of oil)

phrases.english: And if you say: yes, it is indeed so,
but was it not taught: "From evening until morning":
give it its measure of oil,
so that it will keep burning all night
from evening until morning.
Another explanation: "From evening until morning":

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁכְּשֵׁרָה מֵעֶרֶב עַד בֹּקֶר
phrases.english: you have no service that is valid from evening until morning
except this one alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off the possible answer 'yes, light first' to the rhetorical question in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that in the afternoon the lighting must be the last service, after the קטורת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'מערב עד בקר' (שמות כז:כא).

steps.title: Conclusion: 'when' means 'at the time of', in the afternoon and the morning
steps.stepSummary: The afternoon פסוק must mean 'at the time of lighting, burn the קטורת'. So the morning פסוק likewise means 'at the time of the הטבה, burn the קטורת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the Torah saying? At the time of the lighting, the incense should be burned. Here too: at the time of the cleaning of the lamps, the incense should be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It reads the afternoon פסוק as 'at the time of', then applies the same reading to the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The afternoon פסוק cannot mean 'after', so it must mean 'at the time of'. Since the morning פסוק has the same structure, it should be read the same way. This is the רבנן's full argument against אבא שאול.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what is the Torah (literally, the Merciful One) saying?

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, both פסוקים say 'at the time of', not 'after'. So in the morning the קטורת may come before the הטבה, just as in the afternoon it comes before the lighting.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the Merciful One saying?
At the time of lighting, the incense shall be burned.
Here too:
at the time of cleaning the lamps, the incense shall be burned.
phrases.notes: The גמרא isn't starting over. It repeats the opening line from Step 1 on purpose, because that's what the proof just showed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from Steps 2 and 3 and applies it back to Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the רבנן, the morning קטורת is burned at the time of the הטבה and does not have to come after it.

steps.title: אבא שאול's reply: the afternoon is different because of the word 'אותו'
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול can answer that the afternoon case is an exception. The word 'אותו' in the evening פסוק teaches that only there must the lighting come last.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבא שאול would tell you: It is different there, because it is written 'אותו' (it).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives אבא שאול's defense. He says the afternoon proof does not carry over to the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אותו' in 'יערוך אותו אהרן ובניו מערב עד בקר' limits the rule: only the evening lighting must be the final service. Without that word, the morning פסוק keeps its plain order: first the הטבה, then the קטורת. So the רבנן's comparison between morning and afternoon breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: Would say to you (a reply on his behalf)
'It': a limiting word that restricts a rule to this case

phrases.english: And Abba Shaul would say to you:
It is different there, for it is written "it."
phrases.notes: From שמות כז:כא, 'יערוך אותו אהרן ובניו', which limits the rule to the evening lighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל אָמַר לָךְ: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אבא שאול against the רבנן's proof in Steps 2 through 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (שאני) based on a limiting word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The afternoon rule proves how the morning פסוק should be read.
steps.terutzMaskana: The afternoon is a special exception because of 'אותו'. The morning keeps the plain order: הטבה first, then קטורת.

steps.title: רב פפא: the two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא resolves the contradiction between the two משניות. One follows the רבנן and the other follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is not difficult. This one follows the רבנן, and that one follows אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original problem: two משניות that list the order of services differently. רב פפא answers that each משנה follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that puts the קטורת first matches the רבנן's view. The משנה that puts the הטבה first matches אבא שאול. So the contradiction is really just a מחלוקת between תנאים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a standard way the גמרא handles conflicting משניות: it assigns each one to a different תנא instead of forcing them to agree.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is not difficult;
this one follows the Rabbis, that one follows Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the contradiction between the משניות and offers a new resolution based on the מחלוקת just explained.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each משנה to a different תנא (הא רבנן הא אבא שאול)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות come from one source, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משניות reflect two opinions: the רבנן (קטורת first) and אבא שאול (הטבה first).

steps.title: Restating which משנה follows whom, as setup for a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רב פפא's assignment: our משנה follows the רבנן, and the משנה of the פייס follows אבא שאול. This prepares the next challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you establish our משנה here? As the רבנן. And the משנה of the lottery? As אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא spells out exactly which משנה goes with which תנא so it can test that assignment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. Pinning down the assignment lets the גמרא check whether it stays consistent with other details in those same משניות. The real challenge comes in the next step, from the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery: the משנה describing the lottery for assigning services

phrases.english: How did you establish our mishna here? As the Rabbis;
and the mishna of the lottery, as Abba Shaul.
phrases.notes: The sentence continues into Step 8, where the challenge comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out רב פפא's answer from Step 6 to prepare a challenge against it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Confirming exactly which משנה is assigned to which תנא, so the assignment can be tested for consistency.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Our משנה follows the רבנן; the משנה of the פייס follows אבא שאול.

steps.title: The last clause brings us back to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of our משנה puts the קטורת before the נרות, which is the view of the רבנן. So רב פפא's answer leaves our משנה split: the beginning and end follow the רבנן, and the middle follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: 'They brought him the תמיד. He made the main cut, and another כהן finished the שחיטה for him. Then he went in to burn the קטורת and to clean the lamps.' That is the view of the רבנן. So the first and last clauses follow the רבנן, and the middle clause follows אבא שאול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's answer. It points to the end of our משנה, which follows the רבנן, so the משנה ends up switching opinions in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא had said our משנה follows the רבנן. But the middle part of the same משנה follows אבא שאול. That gives a strange pattern: רבנן, then אבא שאול, then רבנן again. Normally we do not like explaining a single משנה as jumping back and forth between opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut it (made the main cut of the שחיטה)
The first clause and the last clause

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
They brought him the daily offering,

phrases.aramaic: קְרָצוֹ וּמֵרַק אַחֵר שְׁחִיטָה עַל יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: he cut it, and another completed the slaughter on his behalf,
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול makes most of the cut, and another כהן finishes it.

phrases.english: he entered to burn the incense
and to clean the lamps —
phrases.notes: קטורת is listed first, then the lamps.

phrases.english: we have arrived at the Rabbis.
The first and last clauses are the Rabbis,
and the middle clause is Abba Shaul!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's assignment of the two משניות, which step 7 restated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's resolution that our משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא follows the רבנן, but the middle follows אבא שאול. That forces an awkward split within one משנה.

steps.title: רב פפא accepts the split
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא agrees: the first and last clauses follow the רבנן, and the middle clause follows אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא can tell you: Yes, the first and last clauses follow the רבנן, and the middle clause follows אבא שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא does not run from the challenge. He simply accepts that the משנה really is split this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is called 'biting the bullet': the 'problem' is accepted as true. The גמרא gives no reason for רב פפא's answer. Some explain that such a split, though uncommon, is possible because these clauses are not right next to each other.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa could have said to you: Yes,
the first and last clauses are the Rabbis,
and the middle clause is Abba Shaul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by accepting its conclusion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A split משנה (רבנן, then אבא שאול, then רבנן) should be impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split is acceptable; רב פפא holds it this way.

steps.title: Why didn't רב פפא use אביי's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why אביי rejects רב פפא's answer, since he does not want a split משנה. But why didn't רב פפא accept אביי's simpler answer?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that אביי did not answer like רב פפא, because he would not explain the first and last clauses by the רבנן and the middle by אבא שאול. But רב פפא, why didn't he answer like אביי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers. It sets up a question: what did רב פפא find wrong with אביי's approach?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reason is clear: he avoids a split משנה. רב פפא chose the harder answer, the split. So he must have seen a problem in אביי's answer, and the גמרא asks what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (introduces a contrast)
Explains it as (following a certain view)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אַבָּיֵי לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: Granted, Abaye does not say like Rav Pappa,
the first and last clauses the Rabbis

phrases.aramaic: וּמְצִיעֲתָא אַבָּא שָׁאוּל לָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ.
phrases.english: and the middle clause Abba Shaul — he will not explain it so.
But Rav Pappa, what is the reason
he did not say like Abaye?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אַבָּיֵי לָא אָמַר כְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב פפא has accepted the split, the גמרא asks why he preferred it over אביי's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem did רב פפא see in אביי's answer?

steps.title: The two lamps come before the five
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects that according to אביי, the רישא would list the cleaning of two lamps before the cleaning of five lamps. In real life the five are done first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: Would the first clause teach the cleaning of two lamps, and only afterward the cleaning of five lamps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב פפא's reason. אביי's reading would make the משנה list things out of their real order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the actual service, five lamps are cleaned first and the last two later. Under אביי's approach, the רישא mentions the two lamps before the five. רב פפא finds that backwards order hard to accept, so he prefers to say the משניות reflect a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning and preparing the lamps of the מנורה

phrases.english: He could say to you: Would it teach in the first clause
the cleaning of two lamps,
and afterward the cleaning of five lamps?
phrases.notes: The five lamps are actually cleaned first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי's answer would make the משנה list the two lamps before the five, which is out of order.

steps.title: The first clause is only a training list
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that the first clause is only a general list of what the כהן גדול must be trained in, not the order. The real order is taught later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי can tell you: The first clause is only giving general instruction. The actual order is taught again later.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his answer against רב פפא's objection. The early list is not meant to show the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the seven days before יום כיפור, the כהן גדול is trained in all the services. The first clause just names those services. The order does not matter there, so listing the two lamps before the five is no problem. The exact order appears later in the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the first clause as a step-by-step order of the עבודה. According to אביי it is only a training checklist.

phrases.english: And Abaye could say to you:
it is merely giving general instruction,
and the order — it teaches it again later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי against רב פפא's objection in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the clause is meant to do
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא lists the services in their real order, so the two lamps come before the five.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא only lists what to train in. The real order is taught later.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי avoids splitting the משנה by reading the רישא as a training list. רב פפא avoids the backwards list by accepting a split משנה.

steps.title: How the blood is sprinkled on the corners of the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: A new topic (גופא): the blood of an עולה is put on the northeast corner and the southwest corner. A ברייתא says that for the תמיד, רבי שמעון איש המצפה has it put on the west side and then the south side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself: He comes to the northeast corner and sprinkles at the northeast. At the southwest corner he sprinkles at the southwest. A ברייתא taught on this: רבי שמעון איש המצפה changes the procedure for the תמיד. He comes to the northeast corner and sprinkles at the northeast. At the southwest, he sprinkles on the west side and afterward on the south side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a source. It then brings a ברייתא with a different view for the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is two sprinklings, one on each of two opposite corners. רבי שמעון איש המצפה says the תמיד is different at the second corner. There the blood goes first on the west side and then on the south side, instead of all at once. This sets up the question of why.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to analyze a quoted source)
And a ברייתא taught on it

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא: בָּא לוֹ לְקֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית —
phrases.english: The matter itself: He comes to the northeast corner —
he sprinkles at the northeast,
the southwest — he sprinkles at the southwest.

phrases.aramaic: וְתָנֵי עֲלַהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה
phrases.english: And it was taught on it: Rabbi Shimon Ish HaMitzpa
changes it for the daily offering,
he comes to the northeast corner —
he sprinkles at the northeast,
the southwest — he sprinkles on the west
and afterward sprinkles on the south.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: בָּא לוֹ לְקֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of קטורת and נרות. Starts analyzing a quoted source about the sprinkling of blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Usually the blood goes on the northeast and southwest corners. רבי שמעון איש המצפה says that for the תמיד, at the southwest corner it goes first on the west side and then on the south side.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון איש המצפה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון איש המצפה treats the תמיד differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון איש המצפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source or logic behind רבי שמעון איש המצפה's special rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule changes the normal sprinkling only for the תמיד. The גמרא wants to know what makes the תמיד different.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal עולה offered morning and afternoon

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon Ish HaMitzpa?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אִישׁ הַמִּצְפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling quoted in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason (source or logic) for treating the תמיד differently at the southwest corner.

steps.title: A verse links the תמיד to a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting a scholar of רבי ינאי's school, says the פסוק places the חטאת goat 'על עולת התמיד.' This teaches that the תמיד, though an עולה, should be done with some of the procedure of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of one of the scholars of the school of רבי ינאי: The verse says, 'And one goat as a חטאת to ה׳, it shall be offered beside the daily עולה and its libation.' The תמיד is an עולה, yet the Torah says: do with it the procedure of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 14. רבי שמעון איש המצפה treats the תמיד differently because a פסוק connects it to a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the חטאת goat right next to the עולת התמיד. From this closeness we learn that the תמיד, while staying an עולה, takes on some of the procedure of a חטאת. The תמיד is still an עולה; it simply has a special way of giving its blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily burnt-offering brought every morning and afternoon
Sin-offering; its blood is put on all four corners of the מזבח, each one separately
Burnt-offering; its blood is given on two opposite corners, so it touches all four sides
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
The procedure or way of doing something

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תמיד stops being an עולה. It is fully an עולה; the פסוק only changes how its blood is given.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם חַד דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of one of the school of Rabbi Yannai:
The verse says:
'And one goat as a sin-offering to ה׳'
'shall be offered beside the daily burnt-offering and its libation.'
It (the תמיד) is a burnt-offering,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: עֲבֵיד בַּהּ מַעֲשֵׂה חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: and the Torah said: perform with it the procedure of a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם חַד דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the תמיד to a חטאת, so its blood is given partly in the way of a חטאת.

steps.title: How to give the blood: half עולה, half חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The method is one corner sprinkling that covers two sides (like an עולה), then two separate sprinklings (like a חטאת).
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this done? He gives one sprinkling that counts as two, the way of an עולה, and two sprinklings that count as two, the way of a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how to carry out the rule from the פסוק. Half the blood is given like an עולה and half like a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal עולה uses two corner sprinklings, and each one covers two sides. Here the תמיד gets only one such corner sprinkling (the עולה half). It then gets two single-side sprinklings, given one by one like a חטאת. These match the west and south sides in the ברייתא of Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this so? How is it done?
One sprinkling that counts as two: put on a corner, it reaches two sides
Two sprinklings that count as two: each touches only one side

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows exactly how the ברייתא of רבי שמעון איש המצפה (west, then south) fits the פסוק.

phrases.english: How is this done?
He gives one sprinkling that is two,
like the procedure of a burnt-offering,
and two sprinklings that are two,
like the procedure of a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to carry out the rule derived in Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One corner sprinkling (the עולה way) plus two single sprinklings (the חטאת way).

steps.title: Why not do a full עולה and then a full חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why split it? Do a complete עולה (two sprinklings that are four), then a complete חטאת (four sprinklings that are four).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him instead give two sprinklings that are four, like an עולה, and then four sprinklings that are four, like a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the half-and-half method. It suggests doing both procedures in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תמיד needs both עולה and חטאת features, the simplest idea is to do each one completely. Splitting each procedure in half seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Two sprinklings that are four: the normal full עולה, two corners covering four sides
Four sprinklings that are four: the normal full חטאת, one on each corner

phrases.english: But let him give two sprinklings that are four
like the procedure of a burnt-offering,
and four sprinklings that are four
like the procedure of a sin-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method given in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The half עולה, half חטאת method
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Doing each procedure in full would seem to satisfy the פסוק better than splitting both.

steps.title: Blood cannot atone twice
steps.stepSummary: There is no case where blood atones and then atones again. A full עולה would already finish the atonement, so a full חטאת after it is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: We never find blood that brings atonement and then brings atonement again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Doing both procedures in full would mean the same blood atones twice, and that never happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the full עולה sprinklings are done, the offering's atonement is complete. Starting a whole new חטאת procedure would be a second atonement, which has no precedent.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found; there is no such case

phrases.english: We have not found blood
that atones and then atones again.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצִינוּ דָּמִים שֶׁמְּכַפְּרִין וְחוֹזְרִין וּמְכַפְּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the proposal because it has no precedent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Do a full עולה and then a full חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not possible, because blood does not atone twice.

steps.title: But half-and-half has no precedent either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: blood that is half חטאת and half עולה is also unheard of. If the פסוק forces that new thing, let it force a double atonement too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we ever find blood that is half חטאת and half עולה? Rather, you must say the verse forced this by linking them. Here too, say the verse forced it by linking them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 18. It points out that the accepted method is also something never seen before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The half-and-half method has no precedent either. We accept it only because the פסוק forces it. So 'we never found it' is not a real argument, and the פסוק could just as well force a full עולה plus a full חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: And did we ever find? (a challenging question)
By force; we have no choice

phrases.english: And did we ever find blood
that is half sin-offering and half burnt-offering?
Rather, by force, the verse linked them.
Here too:
by force, the verse linked them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָצִינוּ דָּמִים שֶׁחֶצְיָין חַטָּאת וְחֶצְיָין עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument 'we never found blood that atones twice'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted method is also without precedent and rests only on the פסוק, so the פסוק could also support a double atonement.

steps.title: Splitting the sprinklings is only a small change
steps.stepSummary: The half-and-half method only splits the normal sprinklings into separate parts. It is not a new kind of atonement, unlike a double atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is merely a splitting of the sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The accepted method is only a minor change, while a double atonement would be a real new thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With half-and-half, the blood still reaches the same four sides as a normal עולה. One corner sprinkling is simply broken into two single-side sprinklings. Atoning twice would be a completely new kind of procedure, so the פסוק is not read that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Splitting the blood sprinklings into separate parts

steps.whatToRemember: The תמיד's blood covers the four sides like an עולה. The second corner sprinkling is just split into two separate חטאת-style sprinklings. A full extra חטאת procedure is not allowed, because blood does not atone twice.

phrases.english: There, it is merely a splitting of the sprinklings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases: a small change versus a brand-new procedure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both methods are equally new, so the פסוק could force either one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting the sprinklings is a minor change; a double atonement is a real innovation and is not done.

steps.title: Why not split by height instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way: give the עולה-style sprinkling below the red line and the two חטאת-style sprinklings above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us give one sprinkling that is two below, like an עולה, and two sprinklings that are two above, like a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. If the תמיד takes on חטאת features, perhaps the חטאת part should also be given high up, the way a חטאת is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of a חטאת is put on the upper half of the מזבח, and the blood of an עולה on the lower half. So the חטאת half of the תמיד should perhaps go above the red line. This would still only be a 'splitting,' not a double atonement. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Below the red line, on the lower half of the מזבח (where עולה blood goes)
Above the red line, on the upper half of the מזבח (where חטאת blood goes)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Below' and 'above' here mean below or above the red line (חוט הסיקרא) halfway up the מזבח. They do not mean the ground or the top surface.

phrases.english: Let us give one sprinkling that is two below (the red line),
like the procedure of a burnt-offering,
and two sprinklings that are two above (the red line),
like the procedure of a sin-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 20 accepts 'splitting,' this asks whether the split should also be by height
steps.kashyaTarget: The method in which all the sprinklings are given at the same height
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A true חטאת-style sprinkling is given above the red line, so the חטאת half of the תמיד should go up there too.

steps.title: Blood is never split between above and below
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 21. We never find one set of blood sprinkled partly above the red line and partly below it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have not found blood that is half sprinkled above and half sprinkled below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the step 21 suggestion. That plan would put the עולה-style sprinkling below the red line and the חטאת-style sprinklings above it. The reason given is that splitting blood between above and below is unheard of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every קרבן's blood goes entirely in one zone. It is either all below the red line, like most קרבנות, or all above it, like a חטאת. Splitting one blood between both zones would be a brand-new kind of service, so the step 21 suggestion fails.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found (there is no precedent for this)
The red line around the middle of the outer altar that divides 'above' from 'below'

phrases.english: We have not found blood
half of which is above and half of which is below.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצִינוּ דָּמִים שֶׁחֶצְיָין לְמַעְלָה וְחֶצְיָין לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative sprinkling arrangement proposed in step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could split the sprinklings between above and below the red line.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting blood between above and below has no precedent, so this option is ruled out.

steps.title: Challenge from the one-up, seven-down sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim using the יום כיפור service. There the כהן גדול sprinkles once upward and seven times downward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really no such case? But we learned in a משנה: He sprinkled from it once upward and seven times downward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule from step 22. It quotes a משנה about the כהן גדול in the קודש הקדשים, which seems to split blood between 'up' and 'down'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one blood is sprinkled both upward and downward, then a split between above and below does exist. That would knock out the reason given in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: One upward and seven downward: the יום כיפור sprinklings toward the כפורת

phrases.english: And is there not? But didn't we learn:
He sprinkled from it one time upward
and seven times downward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'no precedent' claim of step 22 with a counter-example from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood is never split between above and below
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יום כיפור service sprinkles one time up and seven times down, which looks like exactly that kind of split.

steps.title: It was like a whip, all in one row
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the sprinklings were done 'like a מצליף', a person whipping. Each drop lands below the last one in a row, so no zone is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was like one who whips. What does 'like one who whips' mean? רב יהודה demonstrated with his hand: like a person giving lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'up' and 'down' in that משנה describe the direction of the hand motion. They do not describe two separate zones. רב יהודה shows the motion with his hand to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone whipping brings each lash down a little below the previous one. In the same way, the sprinklings landed one beneath the other in a single row. Nothing was split between an 'above zone' and a 'below zone', so the rule from step 22 still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Upward' and 'downward' here describe the angle of the כהן's hand. They are not the 'above/below the red line' zones of the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: Like one who whips.
What does 'like one who whips' mean?
Rav Yehuda demonstrated: like one giving lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 22 against the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One up, seven down' means blood split between an upper and a lower zone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It describes a whip-like motion with drops in a single row, so there is no split.

steps.title: Challenge from the seven sprinklings on the middle of the altar
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge comes from the golden מזבח. The blood is sprinkled seven times 'on its טהרו', which seems to mean its middle. That would put some drops above the middle and some below.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there not? But we learned: He sprinkled from it on the טהרו of the altar seven times. Doesn't this mean the middle of the altar? As people say, 'clear noon' is the middle of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second counter-example from a משנה. It argues that טהרו means 'the middle', using a common saying about noon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If seven sprinklings go on the middle of the altar's side, some will land above that midpoint and some below. That would be blood split between above and below, which contradicts step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'טהר' of the altar: the word whose meaning is debated here
Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: And is there not? But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: הִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: He sprinkled from it on the 'tohoro' of the altar
seven times.
Is it not referring to the middle of the altar,
as people say:
'Clear noon' is the middle of the day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָתְנַן: הִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, this is a second counter-example against step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that blood is never split between above and below
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טהרו means 'middle', seven sprinklings there must land partly above and partly below the midpoint.

steps.title: רבה בר שילא begins: No, that is not the meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא starts to answer by denying that טהרו means 'the middle of the altar'. His explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: No.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the answer to the challenge in step 25. רבה בר שילא rejects the reading 'middle', and the גמרא is about to explain what טהרו really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection targets the translation of the word, not the משנה itself. If טהרו does not mean 'middle', then the second counter-example falls away, and the rule from step 22 is safe.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said: No,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the defense against the challenge of step 25. It continues on the next amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading a word in the משנה (opening only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: טהרו means the middle of the altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: טהרו does not mean the middle. The full explanation follows on the next amud.
